strategyPoints: Tire wear will be a major factor on this abrasive surface, particularly on the front left. Expect to see some strategic variation in pit stops.
With a lap time of just under a minute, the pit window is relatively short here. A perfectly timed stop could be the difference between victory and defeat.
Fuel consumption will be less of a concern on this short circuit compared to longer tracks, allowing teams to focus on other performance aspects.
The short lap length means traffic will be a constant issue, requiring drivers to be assertive when overtaking and patient when navigating slower cars.
Qualifying is absolutely critical here, as overtaking can be challenging on this tight and twisty layout.
The undercut could be a powerful strategy here, with drivers able to gain significant time in clean air after a pit stop.
Managing tire temperatures will be crucial, especially during the early stages of the race and after safety car periods.
A safety car could completely reshuffle the pack, so teams need to be prepared to react quickly to changing circumstances.
weatherCommentary: The altitude here in Ibarra can affect engine performance, with the thinner air reducing horsepower. Teams will be carefully monitoring their power units.

The sun can be intense at this altitude, so tire management will be even more crucial if temperatures rise.

The humidity can be high in Ibarra, which can affect the drivers' concentration and stamina.
